summary: The excerpt demonstrates a Photoshop-based editing workflow aimed at producing a high-dynamic-range look and directing attention toward the sun. It begins with exposure and shadow adjustments to create HDR-like balance, then proceeds to sky manipulation using a trapezoid rule to echo foreground symmetry. The editor uses masking and painting to darken and cool the sky, reintroduce preferred cloud elements, and intensify glow around the sun. A Whites adjustment layer is applied to enhance light, followed by layer flattening to finalize the composition. The steps are presented in a sequential, record-at-this-step style, illustrating practical on-screen edits rather than a generic theoretical discussion.

sections.title: HDR-like exposure balancing and sky manipulation
sections.description: Initial steps blend exposure and shadows to achieve a high dynamic range. The sky is subsequently treated to mirror foreground symmetry using a trapezoid rule, with selective painting and masking to darken/cool certain areas and to preserve or reintroduce preferred cloud elements. The sequence also includes slimming down the background, flattening layers, and applying a Whites adjustment to enhance light toward the sun.
